newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's leu strengthens after last week's dip.
newsitem.headline: Romania's leu strengthens after last week's dip.

text.p: Romania's leu strengthened against the dollar at midday on Monday when it was quoted at about 7,000/300 from around 7,300/450 in early trading on large dollar selling orders, traders said.
"Pressure on the dollar just started and pushed the leu up. It might be a result of leu shortages on the money market," said a trader.
Operators were reluctant to forecast whether the leu would consolidate mid-day gains or ease back again.

Most dealers said the central bank (BNR) was not directly intervening to support the leu, but the currency's upswing might have been triggered by a BNR move to mop up leu funds from the money market earlier in the day.
"I don't think the BNR sold dollars as it did on Friday," said one dealer with a foreign bank.
"But the BNR was certainly on the leu side taking funds and it could have hit some players who rushed then to sell dollars," he added.
Dealers said the BNR intervened on the interbank market on Friday, selling dollars to contain growing pressure on the leu after the currency dipped about 2.5 percent on Thursday.
It helped the leu to recover slightly to about 7,200/400 to the dollar from 7,400/600 before inching down to 7,300/450 at Monday's opening.
